title: More Robot？More Human？
summary: At WRC 2026, Richard Robinson used LimX Dynamics’ LimXTalk to argue against the common fear that robots will simply displace human roles, framing embodied AI instead as a way to free up time for connection, creativity, collaboration, and care. The discussion shifts attention from flashy demos to deployment questions: where robots should be useful first, what happens after prototypes leave the stage, and why humanoid robotics ultimately has to be judged by how it serves people.

extra.full_text: At WRC 2026, Richard Robinson challenged one of the biggest fears surrounding robotics: that machines will take something away from us. His perspective? Robots may give something back—more time to connect, create, collaborate, and care for one another. In the first episode of #LimXTalk, we explore what comes after the demo, where robots should go first, and why the future of robotics ultimately comes back to people. Watch the full conversation. #LimXDynamics #WRC2026 #EmbodiedAI #HumanoidRobotics #LimXTalk

title: Specializing AI for Regulated Industries - How Domyn Uses NVIDIA Nemotron
summary: Regulated industries require full ownership,control and customization of the models they deploy with end-to-end governance, transparency, and auditability.

extra.full_text: Regulated industries require full ownership,control and customization of the models they deploy with end-to-end governance, transparency, and auditability. This livestream explores how Domyn has built and specialized its own models, including a 263B-parameter reasoning model purpose-built for regulated industries and smaller models for specific domains and tasks. We'll walk through the training pipeline: model compression, multilingual continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, leveraging the NVIDIA open source ecosystem. Learn how this approach delivers state-of-the-art results on enterprise tasks like text-to-SQL, knowledge graph extraction, and safety classification, and enable AI that you can own, control and customize, built for the demands of regulated industries.

summary: Vitestro says its autonomous blood-draw robot Aletta has received FDA De Novo authorization, making it the first fully autonomous phlebotomy system cleared through a new U.S. device category.
